atoms.text: This guide configures the Tallyforge Batch Query service to read input files and write query results in a single storage bucket. The bucket is named acme-analytics-data and belongs to account 111122223333. The service runs as the IAM role TallyforgeBatchRole. Input CSV files are stored under the prefix raw/, and result files are written under the prefix results/. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to TallyforgeBatchRole. The policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-data/raw/*, s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-data/results/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a condition limiting s3:prefix to raw/ and results/. The bucket policy is not changed, and it contains no statement that refers to the role. After attaching the policy, submit a test job that reads one file from raw/ and confirm that its output object appears under results/.

This guide configures the Tallyforge Batch Query service to read input files and write query results in a single storage bucket. The bucket is named acme-analytics-data and belongs to account 111122223333. The service runs as the IAM role TallyforgeBatchRole. Input CSV files are stored under the prefix raw/, and result files are written under the prefix results/. Access is granted only through a statement in the bucket's resource-based policy, whose Principal is the role ARN arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/TallyforgeBatchRole. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-data/raw/*, s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-data/results/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a condition limiting s3:prefix to raw/ and results/. No storage permissions are added to the role's identity-based policy. After saving the bucket policy, submit a test job that reads one file from raw/ and confirm that its output object appears under results/.

This guide covers access for the Corvane Log Rollup job, which reads raw application logs and writes hourly aggregates. The bucket is named northwind-app-logs, and the job runs as the IAM role CorvaneRollupRole in the same account as the bucket. Raw log objects are read from the prefix incoming/, and aggregate files in Parquet format are written to the prefix rollups/hourly/. Create an identity-based policy and attach it to CorvaneRollupRole. The policy grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::northwind-app-logs/incoming/*, s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::northwind-app-logs/rollups/hourly/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. The bucket policy is left unchanged, so no bucket-level statement refers to the role. The job's scheduler needs no additional credentials because it assumes the role at launch. Verify the setup by running one hour of data and checking that a Parquet file appears under rollups/hourly/.

This guide covers access for the Corvane Log Rollup job, which reads raw application logs and writes hourly aggregates. The bucket is named northwind-app-logs, and the job runs as the IAM role CorvaneRollupRole in the same account as the bucket. Raw log objects are read from the prefix incoming/, and aggregate files in Parquet format are written to the prefix rollups/hourly/. Edit the bucket's resource-based policy and add one statement whose Principal is the ARN of CorvaneRollupRole. The statement grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::northwind-app-logs/incoming/*, s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::northwind-app-logs/rollups/hourly/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. The role's identity-based policy is left unchanged, so it carries no storage permissions. The job's scheduler needs no additional credentials because it assumes the role at launch. Verify the setup by running one hour of data and checking that a Parquet file appears under rollups/hourly/.

This guide describes access for the Lumio Report Builder, a service that reads curated tables and writes scheduled report files. The service runs as the IAM role LumioReportRole. The bucket is named finance-curated-store, and the role and bucket are in the same account. Curated Parquet tables are read from the prefix curated/sales/, and finished PDF and CSV reports are written to the prefix reports/weekly/. Attach an identity-based policy to LumioReportRole that allows s3:GetObject on curated/sales/*, s3:PutObject on reports/weekly/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket. Scope every resource ARN to finance-curated-store so the role cannot reach other buckets. The bucket policy is not modified. Run the report schedule once manually and confirm that the output files are present under reports/weekly/ with the expected sizes.

The bucket is named finance-curated-store, and the role and bucket are in the same account. Add a statement to the bucket's resource-based policy with the ARN of LumioReportRole as Principal, allowing s3:GetObject on curated/sales/*, s3:PutObject on reports/weekly/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket. Scope every resource ARN to finance-curated-store so the statement covers only this bucket. The role's own identity-based policy is not modified and contains no storage statements. Run the report schedule once manually and confirm that the output files are present under reports/weekly/ with the expected sizes.

This guide sets up the Draywell Ingest Validator, which reads files from a landing area and writes rejected records to a quarantine area. The bucket is named retail-ingest-landing, and the validator runs as the IAM role DraywellValidatorRole. Incoming JSON files are read from the prefix landing/, and records that fail schema checks are written as objects to the prefix quarantine/. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on landing/*, s3:PutObject on quarantine/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. The policy does not include s3:DeleteObject, so the validator cannot remove source files. The bucket policy is not changed. Upload a file containing one malformed record to landing/ and start the validator. Confirm that a single object containing the rejected record appears under quarantine/.

This guide gives an analyst access to run interactive SQL queries through the Vantiq Notebook service and save the results to a bucket. The analyst signs in as the IAM user mreyes, and the bucket is named insights-workspace in the same account. Source datasets are read from the prefix datasets/, and query output is written to the prefix scratch/mreyes/. Attach an identity-based policy to the user mreyes with s3:GetObject on datasets/*, s3:PutObject on scratch/mreyes/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket. Restrict the s3:prefix condition for listing to datasets/ and scratch/mreyes/. The bucket policy is not edited, and no statement in it refers to the user. Run a small query from a notebook and verify that the result file is created under scratch/mreyes/. Other analysts require their own policies and prefixes.

This guide configures the Halcyon Sessionizer to read clickstream events and write session tables, using a role in the bucket owner's account. The bucket is named webmetrics-events and belongs to account 111122223333, and the service runs as the IAM role HalcyonSessionRole in that account. Event files are read from the prefix events/daily/, and session output is written to the prefix sessions/. Attach an identity-based policy to HalcyonSessionRole that allows s3:GetObject on events/daily/*, s3:PutObject on sessions/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. Because the role and bucket share an account, the identity-based policy is sufficient. The bucket policy is not changed. Run the sessionizer for one day of events and verify that session files appear under sessions/. Check that the job log shows no access denied responses.

This guide configures the Halcyon Sessionizer to read clickstream events and write session tables, using a role in a separate processing account. The bucket is named webmetrics-events and belongs to account 111122223333, and the service runs in account 444455556666. Event files are read from the prefix events/daily/, and session output is written to the prefix sessions/. Add a statement to the bucket's resource-based policy with the account ID 444455556666 as Principal, allowing s3:GetObject on events/daily/*, s3:PutObject on sessions/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. The bucket owner's grant is made only in this statement. Administrators of account 444455556666 then delegate it to the service's role. Run the sessionizer for one day of events and verify that session files appear under sessions/. Check that the job log shows no access denied responses.

This guide sets up read-only access for the Brisk Partner Import service, which reads exchange files supplied by a data team and writes load summaries to a second location. The service runs as the IAM role BriskImportRole. It reads Avro files from the prefix inbound/ in the bucket partner-exchange-eu and writes summary JSON files to the prefix import-reports/ in the same bucket. Attach an identity-based policy to BriskImportRole allowing s3:GetObject on inbound/*, s3:PutObject on import-reports/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket. Source files are never modified, so the policy omits s3:PutObject for inbound/ and omits s3:DeleteObject everywhere. The bucket policy is not touched. Place one test Avro file under inbound/ and run an import. Confirm that exactly one summary file appears under import-reports/.

This guide covers the Pallor Compactor, a job that reads many small Parquet files and writes larger merged files. The bucket is named telemetry-lake, and the job runs as the IAM role PallorCompactRole in the same account. Small files are read from the prefix ingest/small/, and merged files are written to the prefix ingest/compacted/ using multipart uploads. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on ingest/small/*, s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on ingest/compacted/*, and s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket. The bucket policy is not changed. Ensure the policy omits s3:DeleteObject, since originals are removed by a separate retention rule. Run a compaction on one partition and verify that the merged file is complete and that no incomplete multipart uploads remain.
